name_reason: The suffix '_60181' is a Ghidra address residue: 0x60181 is the symbol's OWN address (read_memory base / the LEA literal in the sole accessor), exactly the forbidden pattern called out by the naming rule (cf. _52758=0x52758). It is not a domain ID (not a chapter 1-30 / item 00-D6 / spell 00-23 / job 00-1A / portrait 00-41, nor an array dimension/multiplier). Proposed name keeps the compliant data_fd2_ prefix, retains the accurate 'orphan' descriptor (sole consumer is an orphan accessor with 0 static callers / 0 LE-FIXUP targets -- a co-dead data+accessor chain per emission pipeline_spec rule E-7e), adds 'packed3' to convey the 3-byte packed-record stride (the one concrete structural fact known), and keeps 'table' as the data-type descriptor. The name is unique (it is the only 'orphan' symbol in the tree today), so dropping the address loses no disambiguation. Recorded only; Stage 2 applies the rename across globals.h/protos.h and (separately) the matching accessor fd2_get_orphan_table_60181_entry.
purpose: Read-only .object3 table of packed 3-byte records reached only through the orphan accessor fd2_get_orphan_table_60181_entry (0 static callers); its game-side semantics are unknown because no live consumer survives (dead co-dependent data+accessor chain).
logic_summary: 299-byte const uint8 array at 0x60181 in .object3; every byte is a 6-bit value (0x00..0x3F = 0..63). The sole accessor returns (data + idx*3): a raw byte pointer to the idx-th 3-byte record, so element type is uint8 and the record stride is 3. Layout = 99 full 3-byte records (indices 0..98 occupying 0x60181..0x602A9) plus a 2-byte tail (0x602AA..0x602AB); size is pinned by the .object3 boundary to the next symbol data_fd2_battle_item_effect_table @ 0x602AC (0x602AC - 0x60181 = 0x12B = 299). In FD2.LE Ghidra models the region as a single byte[303] symbol based at 0x60181's predecessor 0x6017D, where 0x6017D..0x60180 is a 4-byte zero pad that nothing references; the src array intentionally starts at 0x60181 (the accessor base) and omits that pad, which is harmless because the accessor only indexes forward from base and there are 0 xrefs to 0x6017D. 299 array bytes verified byte-identical to FD2.LE (read_memory 0x60181 len 299).
datatype: const uint8[299] -- packed 3-byte records (stride 3); Ghidra models the enclosing region as byte[303] @ 0x6017D (4-byte zero prefix + this 299-byte body)
element_semantics: Each byte is a 6-bit field value (0x00..0x3F). The accessor groups bytes into 3-byte records via base + idx*3, but the per-field meaning of the three bytes is unknown: the only consumer is a 0-caller orphan accessor, leaving no decompiled access pattern that reveals what the records encode.
comment_original_issue: src comment had an off-by-one record count ('98 full 3-byte records 0x60181..0x602A9'): the range 0x60181..0x602A9 actually holds 99 records (indices 0..98), matching 99*3=297 + 2-byte tail = 299. It also omitted the 4-byte zero pad at 0x6017D..0x60180 that precedes the array in FD2.LE.

issues.title: Co-dead orphan chain is emitted as const data + accessor, but pipeline_spec rule E-7e says it may be skipped
issues.description: rebuild_info/emission/pipeline_spec.md rule E-7e classifies (data_fd2_orphan_table_60181 + fd2_get_orphan_table_60181_entry) as a co-dead data+accessor chain (accessor has 0 callers / 0 LE-FIXUP targets; Watcom keeps both only via mutual reference) and prescribes skip_unreachable_data + skip_unreachable_code (emit neither). The current src DOES emit both (orphan.c defines the table, table.c defines the accessor). This is functionally safe -- emitting extra unreachable const bytes plus a never-called accessor does not change behaviour -- but it is a discrepancy between the documented emit policy and the actual src. Not a correctness/equivalence bug; flagged for the post-workflow emission-policy reconciliation (decide whether to honor E-7e and drop the chain, or update E-7e to record that this chain is intentionally emitted). Out of scope for this comment/name refine.
issues.evidence: rebuild_info/emission/pipeline_spec.md lines 283-303 (rule E-7e, names this exact data symbol/accessor); get_xrefs_to(0x60181) => single DATA xref from 0x4DB92 (the accessor's LEA), 0 other readers; get_function_callers / xrefs of fd2_get_orphan_table_60181_entry @ 0x4DB84 => 0 static callers; src/table/orphan.c + src/table/table.c both emit the chain.

notes: Evidence: get_plate_comment(0x60181) returns no function (data addr, expected). get_xrefs_to(0x60181) = single DATA xref from 0x4DB92 inside fd2_get_orphan_table_60181_entry (its LEA [0x60181]); 0 game-side writers => const confirmed. read_memory(0x60181,299) byte-identical to orphan.c initializer (spot-checked head 01 2D 29 0B... and tail ...32 2F 0A 21 22 35 19). Accessor decompile returns base + idx*3 (Ghidra renders it as data_orphan_6017d_..._unknown + idx*3 + 4 because Ghidra defined a byte[303] symbol at 0x6017D that encloses 0x60181; the +4 is just 0x60181 expressed relative to that 0x6017D base -- functionally identical to the src form data_fd2_orphan_table_60181 + idx*3). Confirmed next .object3 symbol is data_fd2_battle_item_effect_table @ 0x602AC, fixing size at 299.
